rawContainer.why: 87,698 mark occurrences in one JSON; the distilled evidence below is the durable form. The hash identifies the object the harness produced. Every node satisfies end = start + total by construction, so a re-derivation from this file's raw intervals is exact for the nodes quoted here.

theFinding.claim: Every accepted edit on a commit path builds the full 40-Wall mesh set TWICE: once inside plan-apply (the install, keyed on the compile's own geometry object) and again inside the commit's restore, which is a cache MISS because the identity it passes is not the identity the install cached. The second build is also 5-6x more expensive per Wall than the first, for identical content.
theFinding.betweenActionsControl: The same restore between actions hits: unattributed baseline-restore n=75 p50=37.8 ms with restore-mesh-install p50=0.0 ms (curved), n=50 p50=34.6 / 0.0 (straight). The 37.8 ms there is restore-reactive-write, not meshes.
theFinding.notProvedHere: WHY the identity differs is narrowed, not pinned: (a) the app holds the preview state in `$state(...)` (EditorApp.svelte:248) and a reactive read could hand back a proxy of the compile's object, or (b) the geometry installed and the geometry captured are two different objects. An in-process probe of (a) did not reproduce a proxy identity in Svelte 5.56 (a runes harness helper collapsed to a non-reactive value, and the plain-object harness reads the raw object back), so no mechanism is claimed beyond the miss itself. The slice that fixes the miss must first pin which identity is handed to `installWallMeshes`.
